title: This is what my screen looks like today, I'm pretty excited!
author: strawberry-ramune
selftext: Every window is its own copy of the game, and each one has an AI agent working on a different piece of it. As I watch each instance go through it's tests, I'm sending instructions and design info over to claude so it can add them to the work queue. There's a lot of pieces that all have to come together, but so far it's coming together really smoothly! I'm pretty excited!

comments.author: vala_ai
comments.body:
Looks really interesting. I like the style of your game as well :)  
  
You have this all running on one machine correct? How do the agents not conflict when working on potentially overlapping features? More info on how you set it up would be great.

replies.author: TheJotaErre_Twitch
replies.body: Me imagino porque usan copias del juego y luego las junta para volver a partir de ahí puede ser?

replies.author: strawberry-ramune
replies.body: Exactly, each subagent works on it's own copy. When the work is done the new files get pulled over into the main one.

replies.author: strawberry-ramune
replies.body:
Yes, everything runs on one machine! When an agent is spun up, it gets a list of the files it's allowed to work on and a prompt that gives it the goals and the expected results.  

Most of the work is editing script files, and each running copy has the full command suite, so any normal instruction you can send through the console can be scripted by the agent. For every feature added, the agent writes a test, and then uses screenshots and returned data to check that the feature works as expected. Each test run launches its own copy of the game, with its own window, port and save folder, so agents testing at the same time don't interfere.  
  
When they're finished, they run the full test suite, so if anything broke, they can see the errors. 

If the agent spots a problem in a file it doesn't own, it reports the issue back to a coordinator agent. The coordinator passes it to the agent that owns that file, which fixes it and runs its own tests. Then the first agent re-tests to confirm.

replies.author: AmbroSnoopi
replies.body: Pls tell me you use git…

replies.author: strawberry-ramune
replies.body: Of course! The changes only get pushed at the end though, it's not used to separate these instances.

replies.author: AmbroSnoopi
replies.body:
Phew! Now i can breath again 😄

I’ve never tried it, but apprearently the git worktree feature is a good fit for such simultaneous agentic development.

comments.author: Few-Distribution9652
comments.body: How do you deal with the assets? Buy them or create them yourself ?

replies.author: strawberry-ramune
replies.body: Everything is made in house! Textures, patterns, fabrics, and heights/normals are all made with python. The character model is made with Claude + Blender.
